0.headline: NSE IPO lets Narayana Murthy, Azim Premji, others reap almost Rs 30,000 cr in riches
0.heading: NSE IPO lets Narayana Murthy, Azim Premji, others reap almost Rs 30,000 cr in riches
0.intro: Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan, Sunil Kant Munjal of Hero Enterpreise, DMart's Radhakishan Damani, Motilal Oswal's Raamdeo Agrawal and Motilal Oswal are among the other notable inidividuals who will stand to gain, as per Moneycontrol's analysis. Tiger Global and 360 One are the instiutions which will make handsome returns.
0.body:
As the National Stock Exchange (NSE) heads towards one of India's biggest-ever stock market debuts, several of its long-standing investors are choosing to hold on to their stakes rather than sell into the landmark listing.

Two of the biggest names set to benefit are IT stalwarts Infosys' Narayana Murthy and Wipro's Azim Premji.

Premji's family office, Premji Invest, and Murthy's family office, Catamaran, Radhakishan Damani and several other marquee investors are retaining their NSE holdings, which are collectively worth almost Rs 30,000 crore at the IPO's upper price band.

At the upper end of the price band, at Rs 1,785 a share, the holdings covered in this analysis are roughly worth a cumulative Rs 29,400 crore. The group includes private investment firms, family offices and prominent individual investors, several of whom are not selling any shares in the IPO.

Notably, NSE's Rs 22,561 crore initial public offering is entirely an offer for sale of 12.64 crore shares. The National Stock Exchange itself will not receive any proceeds from the issue, with the money going to existing shareholders who are selling their holdings.

At the upper end of the price band, the exchange is valued at about Rs 4.42 lakh crore.

Premji leads

Premji Invest is the largest private investment name in the group. PI Opportunities Fund I, its holding vehicle, owns 5.82 crore shares in the National Stock Exchange. At Rs 1,785 apiece, the stake is worth Rs 10,231.6 crore. The fund is not selling shares in the IPO.

Radhakishan Damani, founder of Avenue Supermarts, which operates DMart, owns 3.9 crore shares in the National Stock Exchange. His holding is worth Rs 6,856 crore at the IPO price, and he is retaining the entire stake.

360 ONE, through its various investment vehicles, holds about 4 crore shares, translating into a combined value of about Rs 7,139.3 crore at Rs 1,785 per share.

Tiger Global, through its investment vehicle, holds 56 lakh shares, worth Rs 999.6 crore at the IPO price.

The shareholder list also includes Catamaran, the investment firm associated with Infosys founder N R Narayana Murthy. Catamaran owns 38.5 lakh shares in NSE worth Rs 687 crore.

Together, these four holdings account for about Rs 25,913 crore of the Rs 29,400 crore aggregate.
More marquee names

The shareholder list also includes several prominent business and market names.
Sunil Kant Munjal, chairman of Hero Enterprise, holds 1.02 crore shares, worth about Rs 1,821.2 crore at the IPO price.

Kris Gopalakrishnan, co-founder of Infosys, holds 94.29 lakh shares, worth roughly Rs 1,683 crore.

Other prominent individual investors include Siddharth Balachandran, Vanaja Sundar Iyer, Siddharth Iyer, Lata Bhanshali, Bharat Taparia, Ignatius Navil Noronha, Dolly Khanna, Raamdeo Agrawal and Motilal Oswal.

A decade in the making

NSE first filed its IPO papers with Sebi in December 2016, but the listing kept getting pushed out amid the co-location controversy and related regulatory proceedings. The prolonged delay meant several early investors did not wait around for the eventual public-market debut.

Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and Norwest Venture Partners had exited their NSE holdings by FY22, while Elevation Capital, then SAIF Partners, also began cashing out. Elevation sold NSE shares worth Rs 580.46 crore in the January-March 2023 quarter, after holding the exchange since 2007.

For those investors, the opportunity to monetise came years before NSE finally reached the IPO stage. Meanwhile, investors that stayed through the long wait are now sitting on substantial paper wealth as the exchange heads for its listing.

Some stay, some sell

The decision to hold is not universal among the National Stock Exchange's large shareholders.
Several institutional and private investors are selling part of their holdings through the IPO while retaining substantial stakes.

Aranda Investments, owned by Singapore's Temasek Holdings, held 11.25 crore shares before the offer and is selling about 1.12 crore shares. It will retain roughly 10.12 crore shares, worth about Rs 18,064 crore at the IPO price.

Mahagony will retain about 8.93 crore shares, worth roughly Rs 15,940 crore, after selling part of its position.

Crown Capital will retain around 4.55 crore shares, worth approximately Rs 8,122 crore, while TA Asia Pacific Acquisitions will retain about 3.23 crore shares, worth roughly Rs 5,766 crore.

MS Strategic, an investment vehicle associated with Morgan Stanley, will retain about 1.88 crore shares, worth around Rs 3,356 crore, after selling 1.1 crore shares.

To be sure, the value of stakes being retained by shareholders who are selling a portion of their holdings through the IPO is not included in the roughly Rs 29,400 crore tally above.

The pattern highlights the different approaches among the exchange's long-standing shareholders. Some are using the IPO to monetise part of their investments, while others are carrying their holdings into the listed market.

A landmark listing

The National Stock Exchange's IPO is the culmination of a decade-long wait for the country's largest exchange to enter the listed market. The issue closed on September 21 after receiving bids for more than 50 crore shares against 8.86 crore shares on offer. It was subscribed 5.71 times, with the qualified institutional buyer portion subscribed 12.68 times.

The shares are scheduled to list on September 24. At Rs 1,785, the IPO values the exchange at about Rs 4.42 lakh crore, making it one of India's largest public offerings and giving its long-standing shareholders a liquid market in which to eventually monetise their holdings.

1.headline: Varmora Granito IPO subscribed 5% so far on opening day; check latest GMP
1.heading: Varmora Granito IPO subscribed 5% so far on opening day; check latest GMP
1.intro: The Gujarat-based ceramic and vitrified tiles manufacturing company, Varmora Granito, has opened its initial public offering (IPO) today, with the issue receiving 5 percent subscription, as of 11:30 am on September 22, according to NSE data.
1.body:
The Gujarat-based ceramic and vitrified tiles manufacturing company, Varmora Granito, has opened its initial public offering (IPO) today, with the issue receiving 5 percent subscription, as of 11:30 am on September 22, according to NSE data.

The Rs 708.02 crore IPO received bids for 16,48,926 shares against 3,39,02,899 shares on offer. Retail investors led the demand, with their portion subscribed 9%, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 2%.

In the grey market, the Varmaro Granito shares were commanding a premium of 3.34 percent on the morning of September 22, as per Investorgain. GMP is an unofficial indicator based on activity in the grey market. It can change before listing and does not guarantee the actual listing price or post-listing returns.

Read Also: Who is Dinesh Thakkar? 12th-pass Angel One founder behind Rs 711 crore luxury tower deal in Mumbai

The three-day issue will remain open until September 24. The IPO has a price band of Rs 140-148 per share and comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 320 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 2.62 crore shares worth around Rs 388 crore.

The minimum lot size is 101 shares, meaning retail investors need to invest at least Rs 14,948 at the upper end of the price band.

The IPO is scheduled to close on September 24, with allotment expected to be finalised on September 25. The shares are scheduled to list on September 29 on the NSE and BSE.

Ahead of the public issue, Varmora Granito raised Rs 212.4 crore through its anchor book on September 21.

The company allotted 1.43 crore equity shares to institutional investors at Rs 148 per share, the upper end of the IPO price band. The anchor participation included Goldman Sachs, Societe Generale, 360 ONE, India Acorn Fund, Turnaround Opportunities Fund, Bharti AXA Life Insurance, LC Pharos Multi Strategy Fund and BNP Paribas Financial Markets, along with domestic mutual funds.

Among the domestic mutual funds participating in the anchor book were ICICI Prudential AMC, Bandhan Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal AMC, JM Financial Mutual Fund and Union AMC.

Of the Rs 320 crore fresh issue, Varmora Granito plans to use Rs 245 crore towards repayment of debt. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Check IPO News Here

The debt repayment component is therefore a key part of the company's plan for the fresh capital being raised through the IPO.

Varmora Granito reported revenue of Rs 1,512.46 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 1,446.03 crore in FY25, according to available financial data. Its profit after tax was reported at Rs 55.09 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 30.77 crore in FY25.

The company manufactures and markets ceramic and vitrified tiles, including glazed vitrified tiles and polished vitrified tiles. It operates manufacturing facilities in Gujarat's Morbi cluster and has a distribution network covering India and overseas markets.

The IPO is being managed by JM Financial, Goldman Sachs (India) Securities and SBI Capital Markets.

2.headline: Orient Cables fixes price band at Rs 258-272, Rs 552-crore IPO to open on September 25
2.heading: Orient Cables fixes price band at Rs 258-272, Rs 552-crore IPO to open on September 25
2.intro: Orient Cables IPO | The company is seeking a valuation of Rs 3,095.3 crore at the upper end of the price band.
2.body:
Orient Cables, a Gurugram-based networking cables and passive networking equipment manufacturer, has fixed the price band at Rs 258–272 per share for its Rs 552-crore initial public offering (IPO).

The company is seeking a valuation of Rs 3,095.3 crore at the upper end of the price band.

The maiden public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 320 crore, while the Nagpal family will sell shares worth Rs 232 crore through an offer-for-sale (OFS).

The IPO will open for public subscription on September 25 and close on September 29, while the anchor book will open for a day on September 24.

IPO share allotment is expected to be finalised by September 30, while trading in Orient Cables shares is expected to commence on the stock exchanges on October 5.

Investors can bid for a minimum of 55 equity shares, with subsequent bids to be made in multiples of 55 shares. Accordingly, the minimum and maximum investment for retail investors in the IPO would be Rs 14,960 and Rs 1,94,480, respectively.

Orient Cables will utilise Rs 91.5 crore of the net fresh issue proceeds for the purchase of machinery and equipment and civil works at its manufacturing facilities, while Rs 155.5 crore will be utilised for debt reduction against total outstanding borrowings of Rs 258.4 crore as of June 2026. The remaining proceeds will be set aside for general corporate purposes.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The company is engaged in the manufacturing of networking, specialty power and optical fibre cables, with a capacity of 8.95 lakh km, as well as wire and cable harness assemblies and allied products such as keystone jacks, power strips and power cords, through two plants in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan.

Orient Cables reported a 0.5 percent year-on-year growth in profit to Rs 53.6 crore for the year ended March 2026, from Rs 53.3 crore in the previous year, partly impacted by subdued operating margins. Revenue during the same period surged 42 percent to Rs 1,171.6 crore from Rs 825 crore.

The company recorded a profit of Rs 32.7 crore and revenue of Rs 489.1 crore in the latest quarter ended June 2026.

Merchant bankers IIFL Capital Services and JM Financial are managing the Orient Cables IPO.
